issue_context.title: Bug: NullReferenceException with ShellFileOperations2
issue_context.body:
Sentry Issue: [FILES-APP-1B](https://files-org.sentry.io/issues/5464643879/?referrer=github_integration)

```
System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
  ?, in void ShellFileOperations2.Dispose(bool disposing)
  ?, in void ShellFileOperations2.Finalize()
```

review_comments: How come this has to be thread safe? Just for my knowledge.
If `Dispose` is called by multiple threads at the same time, the other thread will check `disposedValue` before it becomes true, and the disposal process may be done twice.
Doesn't this class get instantiated in *a* STA thread?
But `Dispose` is public and can be called from any thread. And if a NullReferenceException is thrown here, I can only assume it is because non-thread-safe.
